label: dioicous
definition: A phenotypic sex quality inhering in a bryophyte gametophyte by virtue of its bearing only male or only female gametoecia, the two sexes occurring on separate individual plants.
reason: The meaning is right and it is the bryophyte counterpart of FLOPO:0991072 dioecious. But the text says 'A reproductive quality of' where the parent is phenotypic sex (PATO:0001894), and it does not follow the 'inhering in ... by virtue of' form used by its siblings monoicous (FLOPO:0991280) and autoicous (FLOPO:0991093).

label: monomorphic
reason: The correct opposite of FLOPO:0991092 dimorphic, which has the same parent (morphology) and the same set-of-structures wording. PATO has no 'monomorphic'. 'isomorphic' is an acceptable exact synonym in descriptions.

label: margined
reason: Standard glossary sense (having a distinct border differing in colour or texture, e.g. margined leaves, winged-margined seeds). 'bordered' is a true synonym. PATO has no equivalent, and structure is an acceptable parent.

label: wiry
reason: Matches glossary usage (slender, tough and flexible like wire), and PATO has no term. Texture is a loose parent because the quality mixes slenderness with toughness, but it follows FLOPO practice for tactile/consistency terms. No better single PATO parent exists.

label: callose
reason: Standard sense: bearing calluses (hard, thickened, often pale spots or tips). It is distinct from FLOPO:0991346 callus-tipped, which covers the apex only. 'calleux' is the French equivalent. PATO has no term.

label: appendiculate
reason: Glossary sense (bearing appendages, e.g. appendiculate anthers, petals, or the banner of legumes). The genus-differentia form is fine and PATO has no equivalent.

label: mammillate
reason: Correct sense (nipple-shaped protuberances, blunter than papillae), and 'mamillate' is a valid spelling. It could also sit under rough (PATO:0000700) like tuberculate, but it is also used for a single apical protuberance (e.g. seed or fruit tip), so shape is defensible.

label: flat-topped
reason: Common descriptive term (flat-topped corymbs, crowns, capitula). The definition is clear. PATO flat (PATO:0000407) is about a level surface of the bearer itself, not the level outline formed by distal parts, so a separate class is justified.

label: turgid
reason: Glossary sense (swollen, plump, rounded in section, as opposed to compressed), used for fruits, seeds, perigynia and utricles. PATO swollen (PATO:0001851) is defined as a transient abnormal enlargement, so it does not fit normal taxonomic description. The new class is justified.

label: homogamous
definition: A phenotypic sex quality inhering in an inflorescence by virtue of the bearer's containing flowers of only one sexual kind, such as a capitulum of all bisexual flowers.
reason: Its opposite, heterogamous (FLOPO:0991178), sits under phenotypic sex. The same character must not sit under structure. Also, homogamous has a second botanical meaning (anthers and stigmas maturing at the same time, the opposite of dichogamous). The 'flower' bearer suggests some data use that sense, and this class does not cover it. Those statements should be checked or grounded elsewhere.

label: doubly serrate
reason: Correct sense (serrate teeth bearing smaller teeth). The parent, serrated (PATO:0001206), is right. It is distinct from the more general FLOPO:0991278 doubly toothed (under dentated). The synonyms are standard.

label: spathaceous
reason: Glossary sense (spathe-like, e.g. a spathaceous calyx split down one side or spathaceous bracts). The synonyms fit and PATO has no term.

label: pustulate
definition: A rough quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's surface bearing small, rounded, blister-like elevations, often at the bases of hairs.
reason: The meaning is correct. But its closest sibling, tuberculate (FLOPO:0991060), sits under rough (PATO:0000700). Pustulate is the same kind of surface roughening, so it should sit under rough, not directly under texture.

label: scapiform
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's resembling a scape: a long, leafless or nearly leafless axis arising at or near the base of the plant and bearing flowers at its tip.
reason: The exact synonym 'scapose' does not fit. Scapose describes a plant (whole plant) that bears a scape, while scapiform describes an axis that looks like a scape. The 'whole plant' bearer comes from 'scapose'. Make 'scapose' a related synonym or its own class with a whole-plant bearer. Also, the current definition says the bearer 'is' such an axis rather than resembling one.

label: gynaecandrous
definition: A phenotypic sex quality inhering in an inflorescence by virtue of its bearing both pistillate and staminate flowers on the same axis, the pistillate above the staminate.
reason: Wrong parent. FLOPO:0991037 androgynous is defined as staminate above pistillate on the same axis, and gynaecandrous (as in Carex) is the opposite arrangement, so it cannot be a subclass of androgynous. Make it a sibling under phenotypic sex. The current text also contradicts its parent.

label: proliferous
reason: Glossary sense (producing buds, offshoots or plantlets that form new plants, including proliferous fronds and viviparous spikelets). PATO proliferative (PATO:0002102) is about cell division, not this, so there is no duplicate. Structure is an acceptable parent.

label: bipinnatifid
definition: A pinnatifid quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's lobes being themselves pinnatifid, so that the bearer is twice pinnately incised.
reason: The meaning and parent are right. The phrase 'pinnatifid lobes being themselves pinnatifid' is circular and garbled (the lobes of a pinnatifid leaf are not themselves pinnatifid unless the leaf is bipinnatifid). The new text matches FLOPO:0991307 tripinnatifid.

label: hemi-epiphytic
reason: Correctly covers both primary hemi-epiphytes (start on a host, roots reach the soil) and secondary ones (start in the soil, lose the soil connection). It has the same parent as FLOPO:0991110 epiphytic and is rightly not a subclass of it.

label: pandurate
reason: Correct glossary definition (fiddle-shaped, narrowed on each side below the middle). 2-D shape is the right parent for an outline, and PATO has no term.

label: spine-like
reason: The exact synonym 'spinescent' does not fit. In glossaries it means 'becoming spiny / ending in a spine / somewhat spiny', which overlaps FLOPO:0991210 spine-tipped and PATO spiny (PATO:0001365). Spine-like means 'resembling a spine'. Make spinescent a related synonym, or ground it case by case. The class and definition are otherwise fine.

label: fugacious
definition: A deciduous quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's disposition to fall very early, soon after it is formed or after the structure it subtends opens.
reason: Fugacious (caducous) is a kind of deciduous, and caducous is already grounded to PATO:0001730 deciduous (generic) in the reviewed union pairs. Shedability is only the attribute above it. Also, 'or withering' brings in a second, non-shedding meaning (evanescent), which should be dropped or kept only in the synonym.

label: julaceous
reason: Standard bryological sense (shoots that look like a catkin because of closely imbricate, appressed leaves). Cylindrical is a good parent, and the shoot bearer (stem/branch/whole plant) is right.

label: aphyllopodic
reason: Correct Carex/Cyperaceae sense (lowest leaves of the fertile culm bladeless, culm lateral from beneath the previous year's leaves; opposite of phyllopodic). PATO has no term, and structure is acceptable.

label: parted
reason: Glossary sense (cut more than halfway but not to the base or midrib; between cleft/-fid and divided/-sect). It agrees with FLOPO:0991156 pinnatipartite, and split (PATO:0001786) is a suitable parent. The synonyms fit.

label: glume-like
reason: The definition is clear and PO:0009039 is glume. It is used for chaffy bracts, sepals and perianth parts (e.g. Juncaceae, Restionaceae). PATO has no term.

label: obpyramidal
reason: Correct inverse of PATO:0002336 pyramidal (attached at the apex, base distal). PATO has no obpyramidal. The definition follows genus-differentia.

label: squarrose
definition: A spreading quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being abruptly bent outward from an erect or appressed lower part, so that its free distal part stands out at a wide angle or recurves from the axis, as in phyllaries or moss leaves.
reason: The parent is right. The exact synonym 'squarrose-recurved' does not fit: it is a narrower state (squarrose with recurved tips) and should be a narrow or related synonym. The definition is also too narrow: in phyllaries the bend usually comes partway up or near the tip, above an appressed base, not 'at or near its base'.

label: stipule-like
reason: Follows the 'X-like' resemblance pattern. PATO has no such term. 'stipuliforme' is a usable flora-language synonym, like the other French or Latin synonyms.

label: phyllopodic
definition: A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's lowest leaves bearing well-developed blades, the shoot usually arising from the centre of a tuft of leaves rather than laterally from beneath the leaves of a previous shoot.
reason: The meaning is right (as in the Carex usage), but arising from the centre of a leaf tuft is usual, not part of what defines the term. Hedge it and contrast it with its sibling FLOPO:0991233 aphyllopodic. Also use the standard 'bearer's' form.

label: dolabriform
reason: Matches the glossary sense: hatchet- or axe-head-shaped, narrow at the base and widening to a broad, oblique, curved edge. PATO has no such term.

label: biternate
reason: Correct (3 primary divisions, each divided into 3). Consistent with its sibling FLOPO:0991362 triternate. PATO:0000410 pinnate does not cover ternate division.

label: collenchymatous
definition: A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being made of, or containing, collenchyma: living cells whose primary walls are unevenly thickened, usually at the corners where the cells meet.
reason: The flora bearers are organs (leaf, capsule wall), where the term means 'made of or containing collenchyma'. The current text describes single cell walls and is too narrow. Corner thickening is the usual type, not the only one. The exact synonym 'thickened at the corners' should become related.

label: septate-nodulose
reason: Standard term for Juncus and Cyperaceae leaves and stems: cross-walls inside show on the surface as nodules. The definition is correct.

label: colonial
reason: Correct, and distinct from FLOPO:0991007 caespitose (a dense tuft from one base) because the shoots spread vegetatively. Sits correctly under 'aggregated'.

label: anadromous
reason: Correct fern-glossary sense: the first segment or vein of each pinna arises on the side toward the frond apex. Fits under spatial pattern.

label: pinnately branched
reason: Correct. It is not a duplicate of PATO:0000410 pinnate, which is about leaflets on either side of an axis, not branches.

label: flagelliform
reason: Correct: long, slender, whip-like, tapering, as in flagelliform branches and inflorescences. PATO has no such term.

label: mitrate
reason: Matches the moss-calyptra sense (conic, not split down one side, unlike cucullate). Hollow, so 'concave 3-D shape' fits. The fruit and achene bearers are probably mapping noise.

label: hair-pointed
reason: Correct (piliferous, as in moss leaves). Sits under PATO pointed like its sibling FLOPO:0991210 spine-tipped.

label: abortive
reason: PATO:0000588 vestigial ('a remnant structure from earlier development or evolution') already covers structures that stopped developing. 'abortive' should sit under vestigial rather than under the general 'structure'. Flora usage also mixes two senses: reduced but present, and failing to develop at all (as in 'ovules abortive').

label: prorulose
reason: Correct moss-glossary sense: cell ends project above the surface. PATO has no such term.

label: synoicous
reason: Correct bryophyte sexual system, consistent with its siblings autoicous, dioicous and monoicous. 'synoecious' is an accepted variant.

label: excurved
reason: Correct. Distinct from PATO:0002211 recurved (curved backward or downward). PATO has no excurved.

label: tooth-like
bearers: sepal|leaf lamina lobe|leaf sheath auricle|stamen|portion of secretory tissue|keel
reason: Follows the resemblance pattern. It describes a whole structure shaped like a tooth, not a toothed margin (PATO:0001205 dentated), so it is not a duplicate.

label: cyme-like
definition: A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's branching resembling that of a cyme, the main axis ending in a flower and later flowers arising on lateral branches below it.
reason: Inflorescence branching is about structure, not shape, so PATO:0000052 is the wrong parent. 'cymose' (being a cyme) is not the same as 'cyme-like' and should not be attached here, even as a related synonym.

label: spinose-serrate
reason: The class and its definition are correct. The exact synonym 'spinulose-serrate' does not fit: it means teeth ending in minute spines, a narrower sense, and should be narrow or related.

label: polygonal
reason: PATO has no polygonal term. It is the natural parent for PATO hexagonal and pentagonal (both under 2-D shape). The definition is correct for seeds and stem cross-sections.

label: autotrophic
reason: Not in PATO. Fits the trophic quality definition and contrasts with FLOPO parasitic and mycoheterotrophic.

label: diadelphous
reason: Correct (filaments united in two groups, typically 9+1 in Fabaceae). Sits correctly under connate.

label: distylous
reason: Correct two-morph heterostyly (pin and thrum flowers), sibling of tristylous.

label: neuter
reason: The definition and the parent 'sterile' (a fertility quality) are right. But the exact synonym 'asexual' does not fit: in botany 'asexual' means reproducing without sex (by spores or vegetative growth), not a flower with no working sex organs. Remove it, or at most make it a related synonym. A neuter lemma or ray flower is an empty or sterile one, so those bearers fit.

label: septifragal
reason: Matches the standard glossary meaning: the valves break away from the septa, which stay on the central column. 'dehiscent' is the right parent, alongside septicidal and loculicidal.

label: latiseptate
reason: Correct, as used in Brassicaceae: the fruit is flattened parallel to the septum, so the septum spans the widest diameter (the opposite of angustiseptate). 'flattened' is the right parent. PATO has no such term.

label: chasmogamous
reason: Correct, and the open counterpart of FLOPO:0991176 cleistogamous (which sits under 'closed'). The 'seed' bearer means a seed from a chasmogamous flower; that is a data-mapping question, not a fault in the class.

label: parasitic
reason: Correct, and it uses the same parent as FLOPO:0991334 hemiparasitic. PATO has no 'parasitic'. Because this definition says 'wholly or in part', hemiparasitic should become a child of this class; that change belongs to hemiparasitic.

label: monocarpic
reason: The definition and parent are fine and semelparous is a good synonym. 'hapaxanthic' is not an exact synonym: it describes a single stem that dies after flowering. In clustering palms such as Caryota, the stems are hapaxanthic but the plant as a whole lives on. Make it a related synonym.

label: medifixed
reason: The definition is right and matches its siblings basifixed, dorsifixed and peltate. Two synonyms do not fit. 'medifixed hair' names a part plus a quality, not a quality: remove it. 'malpighian' applies only to T-shaped hairs (trichomes attached at the middle): make it a related synonym.

label: clonal
definition: A multi-cellular organismal disposition inhering in a plant by virtue of its spreading vegetatively, by rhizomes, stolons, root suckers or bulbs, into a group of genetically identical shoots or ramets.
reason: Forming clones describes how a plant grows and reproduces (a tendency of the whole plant, like monocarpic), not its shape or build. So PATO:0000141 'structure' is the wrong parent. The meaning is right; the text is reworded to fit the new parent.

label: hypogynous
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being inserted, or bearing the perianth and stamens inserted, on the receptacle below the ovary and free from it.
reason: The meaning and parent are right, but the text says 'a floral organ or flower' and then always describes the perianth and stamens. That reads wrongly when the bearer is a stamen, a perianth part or a disc. The new wording covers both the flower and its organs, in the same style as half-inferior.

label: palmatipartite
definition: A palmately lobed quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being cut palmately more than halfway, but not fully, to the base into segments radiating from a common point.
reason: Wrong parent. Its pinnate counterpart FLOPO:0991156 pinnatipartite sits in the lobed family (under pinnatifid, which is under pinnately lobed). The matching place here is palmately lobed. Palmatifid (FLOPO:0991351) can't be the parent because it is defined as 'about halfway' only. A split depth of 'more than halfway but not to the base' also falls inside palmately divided (FLOPO:0991272).

label: barrel-shaped
reason: Correct 3-D shape (doliiform), and 'convex 3-D shape' is the right parent, the same as for PATO cylindrical-type shapes. PATO has no barrel-shaped term.

label: palmately divided
reason: Its definition ('more than halfway') overlaps palmatipartite and palmatisect, and both related synonyms are already their own classes. palmatisect is FLOPO:0991282, and palmatifid is FLOPO:0991351, which is defined as 'about halfway' and so falls outside this definition. Remove both synonyms. Either keep this as a general class with palmatipartite and palmatisect under it, or use it for 'palmatisect' as many glossaries do.

label: incumbent
definition: A positional quality inhering in a cotyledon by virtue of the cotyledon's back lying against the radicle, which is folded along it.
reason: The cotyledon meaning (notorrhizal, the counterpart of accumbent FLOPO:0991331) is correct. But the 'anther' bearer is a different meaning: an anther turned inward against the filament. That is two meanings in one class, so map anther statements elsewhere. Also: notorrhizal is listed as both an exact and a related synonym; the wording should match accumbent's.

label: pseudopeltate
reason: Correct for fern rhizome scales (attached just inside the base, with overlapping basal lobes, so they look peltate). It sits correctly beside peltate under 'attachment quality'.

label: semi-elliptic
reason: A clear 2-D outline, built like PATO:0002232 semicircular. PATO has no such term.

label: phyllodioicous
definition: A dioicous quality inhering in a bryophyte gametophyte by virtue of its dwarf male plants growing epiphytically on the leaves or tomentum of the female plants.
reason: Phyllodioicy is a kind of dioicy (separate male and female plants, with dwarf males on the females). It belongs under FLOPO:0991211 dioicous, not directly under 'phenotypic sex'. The current text is also not in the 'X quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of...' form.

label: locellate
reason: Correct: anther locules divided by septa into smaller chambers (locelli). 'structure' is a reasonable parent. The 'fruit' bearer is a data-mapping question.

label: doubly toothed
reason: Correct, as the general class above doubly serrate. PATO:0001205 dentated has 'toothed' as a synonym, so the parent fits. FLOPO:0991221 doubly serrate could be placed under it (its serrated parent sits under dentated in PATO).

label: gonioautoicous
reason: Correct: bud-like male structures in leaf axils just below the female ones, on the same stem. It is a form of autoicy, so the parent is right.

label: monoicous
reason: Correct as the bryophyte counterpart of monoecious. It is the umbrella term for autoicous, synoicous and paroicous, so FLOPO:0991093 autoicous and FLOPO:0991252 synoicous should become its children (a fix to those classes, not this one).

label: bistratose
reason: Correct, and the counterpart of FLOPO:0991320 unistratose (which sits under unstratified). 'stratified' is the right parent.

label: palmatisect
reason: Correct, and built the same way as FLOPO:0991155 pinnatisect under PATO:0104362 dissected.

label: glandular-scaly
reason: Correct: covered with peltate glandular scales; glandular-lepidote is a valid synonym. 'scaly' is the right parent.

label: bipinnatisect
reason: Correct and consistent with pinnatisect, just as bipinnatifid sits under pinnatifid.

label: polygamodioecious
definition: A polygamous quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its belonging to a species whose individuals bear either staminate or pistillate flowers together with some bisexual flowers, so that the species is functionally dioecious.
reason: The meaning and parent are right, but the current text describes a single plant even though the term describes the whole species. The new wording uses the species-level form of FLOPO:0991342 gynodioecious.

label: ternately compound
definition: A structural quality inhering in a compound leaf by virtue of the leaf's primary divisions or leaflets being borne in threes from a common point of the axis.
reason: The meaning is right, but 'each of which may again be divided into three' mixes in the meaning of FLOPO:0991241 biternate and FLOPO:0991362 triternate. Those two should become subclasses of this class, and FLOPO:0991161 trifoliolate is the simplest case of it. The exact synonym 'ternate' is risky: in floras 'leaves ternate' often means whorled in threes, a position meaning, not a compound leaf. Make it a related synonym or have curators check those statements.

label: strobiliform
reason: Matches the glossary meaning (cone-like, with crowded overlapping scales or bracts). It is not a duplicate of PATO:0002021 conical, which is only a geometric shape with no scales.

label: bud-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's resembling an unopened bud: small, compact, ovoid or globose, with its parts closely enveloping one another.
reason: The current text needs 'leaves or bracts', which does not fit perianths, gemmae or whole plants in the bearer list. Speaking of the bearer's parts in general covers every case.

label: obpyriform
definition: A convex 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being inversely pear-shaped, broadest at or near the point of attachment and tapering towards the free end.
reason: The definition is backwards. Pyriform means pear-shaped and attached at the narrow end (Stearn), and obpyriform is the reverse, attached at the broad end, as with obpyriform perithecia narrowing into an upper neck. As written, the text describes pyriform (PATO:0005002 pear shaped). The parent is fine.

label: intrapetiolar
reason: Correct glossary meaning for stipules: in the axil between petiole and stem, often joined into one. Naming the bearer follows the pattern of the biternate row. Note that 'intrapetiolar bud' (a bud hidden in the petiole base, as in Platanus) is a different sense that is not covered here.

label: pseudoterminal
reason: Correct: the structure looks terminal but grows from the side, in the axil of the top leaf, after the shoot tip stops or is pushed aside. Well formed, and PATO has no such term.

label: shield-shaped
reason: Clypeate and scutate correctly mean shield-shaped. This is a shape term and is distinct from FLOPO:0991107 peltate, which is about where the stalk attaches. PATO has no such class.

label: equitant
reason: Correct (as in Iris): leaves folded lengthwise, each straddling the next, in two ranks. Spatial pattern is a suitable parent. 'Petiole' in the bearer list is probably an extraction mix-up, not a problem with the definition.

label: paroicous
definition: A monoicous quality inhering in a bryophyte gametophyte by virtue of its antheridia and archegonia being borne in the same gametoecium but not mixed, the antheridia naked in the axils of leaves below the archegonia.
reason: Wrong parent. In bryology, paroicous is one kind of monoicous (along with autoicous and synoicous), and FLOPO:0991280 monoicous now exists. The definition should also say 'bryophyte gametophyte' and 'gametoecium' like its siblings, and should state that the two organs are not mixed, which sets it apart from synoicous. FLOPO:0991093 autoicous and FLOPO:0991252 synoicous should move under monoicous too.

label: rhizautoicous
reason: Correct bryological meaning: the male shoots are joined to the female plant only by rhizoids. A sound subclass of FLOPO:0991093 autoicous.

label: anatropous
reason: Correct: the ovule is turned back, the micropyle sits next to the attachment point, and the stalk is fused along the side as a raphe. It fits under PATO:0000625 inverted ('reversed in position'). 'Leaflet' in the bearer list is an extraction error to fix in the data, not in the class.

label: necked
reason: Correct and well formed. Distinct from beaked (FLOPO:0991028), which ends in a tapering point rather than a short cylindrical neck.

label: petiole-like
reason: Synonym does not fit. 'Pseudopetiolate' describes a leaf that has a false petiole, so its bearer is the leaf. 'Petiole-like' describes the narrowed part itself. Making them exact synonyms mixes two meanings with different bearers. Make 'pseudopetiolate' a related synonym or its own class with a leaf bearer, and keep this class for the narrowed part. 'Petiole' in the bearer list makes no sense with this class.

label: medial (sensu botany)
reason: Correct fern meaning for sori placed about halfway between the costa and the margin. It is not a duplicate of PATO:0001191 'medial to', which is a relation. Keeping 'median' as a related synonym only is right, because 'median' usually means on the midline.

label: systylious
reason: Correct moss meaning: the lid stays attached to the top of the central column and is lifted with it. Well formed. Bearers mapped as 'capsule fruit' or 'fruit' are a mapping issue with the moss capsule, not a problem with the definition.

label: umbilicate
reason: Correct: a small, navel-like dent in the centre. Concave 3-D shape is a suitable parent, and PATO has no such class.

label: runcinate
reason: Correct (as in Taraxacum): pinnately lobed with sharp lobes pointing back towards the base. Pinnately lobed is the right parent.

label: eucamptodromous
definition: A camptodromous quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's secondary veins curving upwards towards the margin and gradually fading out there without joining one another in prominent loops.
reason: Wrong parent. In Hickey's leaf-vein system, eucamptodromous is a type of camptodromous, and FLOPO:0991368 camptodromous now exists. The definition itself is correct.

label: stellate-lepidote
reason: Correct: covered with stalk-centred scales whose edges split into star-like arms. A sound subclass of PATO:0001804 scaly.

label: praemorse
reason: Correct glossary meaning: ending abruptly and raggedly, as if bitten off. It fits under PATO:0000936 truncated ('as if having an end cut off').

label: napiform
reason: Correct: turnip-shaped, broad and rounded above, then sharply narrowed below. PATO has no such class. 'Radish-shaped' is a loose but acceptable synonym.

label: tripinnatifid
reason: Correct, and consistent with its sibling FLOPO:0991227 bipinnatifid under FLOPO:0991078 pinnatifid.

label: trilete
definition: A structural quality inhering in a spore by virtue of the spore's having a three-armed (Y-shaped) scar (laesura) on its proximal face.
reason: Wrong parent, by inconsistency. Its sibling FLOPO:0991343 monolete sits under PATO:0000141 structure, while this one sits under shape. The laesura is a scar on the surface, not the spore's overall shape, so both should sit under structure. The meaning is correct.

label: semi-woody
reason: Synonym does not fit. 'Suffrutescent' is a growth-form term (a plant that is slightly woody at the base, a subshrub), so its bearer is the whole plant. It is not a texture of stems or roots, and should be a related synonym. 'Semi-ligneous' and 'subwoody' are fine. The definition itself is correct.

label: pseudoverticillate
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a set of lateral structures by virtue of their appearing whorled although they are not inserted at a single node, being either crowded on very short internodes or borne in opposite axillary clusters that together encircle the axis.
reason: 'Inserted singly' is too narrow. It leaves out the most common flora use, the false whorls of Lamiaceae flowers (verticillasters), which come from paired clusters in opposite leaf axils. The class is distinct from PATO:0001951 whorled.

label: cruciform
reason: This is the standard glossary meaning (four arms at right angles, e.g. Brassicaceae corollas and cross-shaped hairs). PATO has no cruciform term; PATO:0001953 decussate is about leaf arrangement, not outline. The synonyms fit.

label: tunicate
reason: The definition is correct for bulbs and corms with tunics, and PATO has no such term. FLOPO already has the part 'tunic' (FLOPO:0986041), so a has-part rule could also express this. The class itself is sound.

label: horn-shaped
definition: A 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being elongated, tapering to a point and usually curved, like an animal horn.
reason: Wrong parent. A curved, tapering horn is not a convex 3-D shape in PATO's sense, because a line between two points can fall outside the object. The general PATO:0002266 '3-D shape' fits. The definition text is otherwise fine.

label: urticating
definition: A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being a stiff hair with a brittle, easily broken tip that, on contact, breaks off and injects an irritant fluid into the skin.
reason: The current text has two bearers: the hair, plus 'said of a plant or part that bears such hairs'. A plant or leaf that is urticating should be expressed as having urticating trichomes (has-part), not by the same quality. The meaning for hairs is right.

label: coronate
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's bearing at its apex a crown, a short ring-like rim or circle of small teeth, scales or bristles, often formed by a persistent calyx limb or pappus.
reason: The 'crowned' sense (e.g. achenes or fruits topped by a persistent calyx rim) is right, and the rewrite only makes the crown's makeup clearer. When the pappus itself is called coronate, it means the pappus is crown-shaped. That should go to PATO:0040006 'crown like', not to this class.

label: abruptly narrowed
reason: The synonym 'contracted' does not fit as an exact synonym. In floras 'contracted' mostly means a dense, narrow inflorescence (e.g. a contracted panicle) or shortened, not a sudden narrowing of a blade. Make it at most a related synonym and keep 'abruptly contracted' and 'brusquement rétréci' as exact. The definition itself is fine.

label: saxicolous
reason: Correct meaning (growing on rocks or in rock crevices). The position parent matches its siblings epiphytic, terrestrial and aquatic (FLOPO:0991110-0991112). The synonyms lithophytic, rupestral, epilithic and rupicole fit.

label: semiovate
reason: Standard meaning of half-ovate (one half of an ovate outline, cut lengthwise), and the definition is well formed. PATO has only semicircular (PATO:0002232).

label: root-climbing
reason: Correct: the plant climbs by clinging with adventitious roots along the stem (e.g. ivy, many Araceae). It is properly placed under climbing (FLOPO:0991108).

label: unistratose
reason: Correct bryological usage (a lamina or margin one cell thick). Being one layer thick fits under PATO 'unstratified' (lacking a layered configuration). Monostratose is a correct synonym.

label: pseudolateral
reason: This is the standard Cyperaceae/Juncaceae usage: a terminal inflorescence pushed aside by a lowest bract that looks like the stem continued. PATO has nothing equivalent.

label: bipinnatipartite
reason: Correct, and it follows the pinnatipartite parent's pattern (twice pinnately parted).

label: cladautoicous
reason: Correct bryological meaning: male structures on their own short branch of the same plant, as against gonioautoicous (bud-like in a leaf axil). It is properly placed under autoicous.

label: induplicate
reason: The definition covers both standard uses: induplicate-valvate aestivation (margins folded inward) and induplicate (V-shaped) folding of palm leaves. Folded is a suitable parent.

label: rhizome-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's resembling a rhizome in form: an elongate, thickened, more or less cylindrical axis, often bearing scale leaves or nodes.
reason: The current text puts position and habit ('horizontal, usually subterranean') into a shape quality. Those belong to a separate position or orientation quality. Keep only what is about form.

label: obtrapeziform
reason: Correct 'ob-' inversion of trapeziform (the wider parallel side at the apex), properly placed under PATO:0002044 trapezoid.

label: pleiochasial
reason: Correct: a cyme with more than two branches below each terminal flower, as against dichasial and monochasial. Branched is a suitable parent, and polychasial is an exact synonym.

label: intramarginal
reason: Correct for intramarginal veins and sori (just inside the margin and running along it). PATO has no such term.

label: collateral
reason: Correct standard meaning (side by side at the same level, e.g. collateral ovules or collateral buds). The ovule example helps.

label: gynobasic
reason: Correct (Lamiaceae and Boraginaceae: the style arises from the base between the ovary lobes). The stamen and spike bearers look like extraction noise but do not affect the class.

label: accumbent
reason: Correct Brassicaceae meaning: the radicle lies against the edges of the cotyledons, as against incumbent, where it lies against the back of one cotyledon.

label: paracytic
reason: Matches the standard stomatal-type definition (subsidiary cells parallel to the guard cells). 'Rubiaceous' is correctly only a related synonym.

label: drupe-like
reason: The exact synonym 'drupaceous' does not fit. In floras it is used for true drupes as often as for drupe-like fruits, while this definition excludes true drupes. Make 'drupaceous' a related synonym. The definition is otherwise sound.

label: hemiparasitic
definition: A parasitic quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its being green and photosynthetic while drawing water and mineral nutrients from a host plant through haustoria.
reason: Wrong parent. FLOPO:0991265 'parasitic' (trophic quality, 'wholly or in part') now exists, and hemiparasitic is a kind of it. The definition text is correct.

label: decompound
reason: Correct glossary meaning (divided or compound more than once, e.g. bi- or tripinnate leaves, repeatedly branched panicles). PATO has no compound or decompound value.

label: trullate
reason: Matches standard usage (trowel-shaped, broadest below the middle, lower sides shorter). 2-D shape is the right parent: PATO rhomboid (PATO:0001938) is defined as an oval, spheroid shape, and a trullate outline is not a parallelogram. Its mirror term obtrullate should sit under the same parent.

label: complanate-foliate
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's leaves spreading in one plane, so that the leafy shoot appears flattened.
reason: The synonym does not fit: in most floras 'complanate' on its own means flattened (complanate stems, petioles, seeds), which is PATO flattened (PATO:0002254), so as an exact synonym it would send those statements to this class. Keep 'complanate' only as a related synonym, or match it to this class only when the leaves or the leafy shoot are the subject. Leaf is not a proper bearer; the shoot is.

label: helicoid
reason: Correct for a helicoid cyme (bostryx): successive branches on the same side, so the sympodium curves in a helix; bostrychoid is a true synonym. The coiled parent matches the sibling scorpioid (FLOPO:0991179).

label: catadromous
reason: Matches fern usage: the first segment or vein of each division is basiscopic. The opposite is anadromous. Position is a suitable parent.

label: sour
reason: The class and definition are right, and PATO has bitter (under flavourful) but no sour. The synonyms do not fit as exact: 'acid' clashes with PATO acidic (PATO:0001429, a pH quality), and 'acidulous'/'acidulé' mean slightly sour. Make acidulous, acidulé and acid related synonyms; keep tart as exact.

label: interpetiolar
reason: Standard usage (e.g. Rubiaceae stipules), well formed. It is the counterpart of intrapetiolar (FLOPO:0991290).

label: gynodioecious
reason: Correct: female plants and bisexual (hermaphrodite) plants in the same species. Matches the phenotypic sex siblings (dioecious, andromonoecious). Flower is not a proper bearer; the plant is.

label: monolete
reason: The definition is correct, but the parent is inconsistent with its sister term trilete (FLOPO:0991308), which is under shape (PATO:0000052). Monolete and trilete describe the same feature (the form of the laesura), so they need one parent. Either move monolete to shape, or move both to structure.

label: acrostichoid
reason: Correct: sporangia spread over the whole lower surface of the fertile lamina, not in discrete sori (as in Acrostichum). Spatial pattern is a good parent.

label: ancipitous
reason: Standard: flattened, with two sharp or narrowly winged edges (two-edged). Flattened is the right parent.

label: callus-tipped
bearers: leaf lamina tooth|leaf|leaflet|leaf lamina lobe|leaf lamina|sepal
reason: Correct and well formed; callous-pointed is a true synonym.

label: sympodial
reason: Correct description of sympodial growth (each lateral takes over when the apex before it stops growing). Branched is an acceptable parent; it is the counterpart of monopodial.

label: starchy
reason: Correct; amylaceous is the glossary synonym. Composition is the right parent. PATO has no such term.

label: semicordate
reason: PATO heart shaped allows 'a sinus or rounded lobe at the base', so a base that is cordate on one side only fits under it. The definition matches the glossary (half-cordate, a basal lobe on one side).

label: tetradynamous
reason: Correct (Brassicaceae: six stamens, four long and two short), and the definition rightly names the androecium as the bearer. Annotations are to 'stamen', so the mining should map them to the androecium.

label: palmatifid
reason: Correct (palmately cut about halfway to the base) and consistent with pinnatifid under pinnately lobed.

label: semisagittate
reason: Correct and well formed; it parallels the other half-shapes.

label: obtrullate
definition: A 2-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's outline being shaped like an inverted trowel: angular at base, sides and apex, broadest above the middle, with the two upper sides shorter than the two lower sides.
reason: Wrong parent. PATO rhomboid (PATO:0001938) is defined as 'a spheroid quality ... oval and a little angular in the middle', which does not describe a trowel outline, and its mirror term trullate (FLOPO:0991336) is under 2-D shape. Move it to 2-D shape, with a definition written to mirror trullate's.

label: extrastaminal
reason: Correct: a disc or nectary outside the stamens. Position is a good parent.

label: monopodial
reason: Correct and the counterpart of sympodial.

label: obreniform
reason: Correct (kidney-shaped, attached at the rounded side, notch at the far end). PATO reniform does not fix where the notch is, so it can be the parent. Note that obcordate was placed under 2-D shape instead; aligning the two would be cleaner.

label: extravaginal
reason: Correct grass and sedge usage (innovations break through the base of the sheath); it is the counterpart of intravaginal.

label: vesicular
reason: Two meanings in one class: 'vesiculose'/'vesiculate' mean covered with small bladder-like vesicles (a texture), but 'vesicular' in floras is mostly used of calyces and fruits to mean bladdery or inflated, a shape (PATO inflated). The calyx and fruit bearers suggest the second sense. Either limit the class to the surface sense (label vesiculose, with vesicular as a related synonym) or file 'vesicular calyx/fruit' under inflated.

label: stolon-like
reason: Follows the existing '-like' resemblance pattern under shape and the meaning is right. Its horizontal growth is also about orientation, and the tuber and root bearers are doubtful, but the class is usable.

label: saprophytic
definition: A trophic quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its lacking or nearly lacking chlorophyll and obtaining its carbon and nutrients from soil fungi associated with its roots, which in turn take them from dead organic matter or from other plants.
reason: Flowering plants called 'saprophytes' in floras are mycoheterotrophs: they do not take up dead organic matter themselves. The current text mixes the two ideas. Holomycotrophic (FLOPO:0991374) overlaps and should become a subclass of this class.

label: trisyncolpate
reason: Correct: syncolpate means the colpi meet (fuse) at the poles; PATO has no aperture terms. Structure is an acceptable parent, like the other pollen and leaf-division structure values.

label: triternate
reason: Standard meaning (thrice ternate); same form and parent as its sibling FLOPO:0991241 biternate; PATO has no ternate terms.

label: sordid
reason: Glossaries give sordid as dull, dingy, dirty-looking, usually of a whitish colour; PATO has no such colour value. 'dirty white' fits the usual floristic use.

label: sausage-shaped
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being elongate and cylindrical with rounded ends, straight or slightly curved, like a sausage.
reason: Meaning and synonym allantoid are right, but a curved sausage (the usual sense of allantoid) is not a convex body, so convex 3-D shape (PATO:0002007) is the wrong parent. Move it to shape (PATO:0000052).

label: evenly spaced
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being separated from the neighbouring structures of its kind by about equal distances.
reason: Meaning right, and PATO has no such value, but the text names 'a set of structures' as the bearer and does not follow the 'by virtue of the bearer's' form. Rewritten so the quality inheres in each member, as with PATO:0001952 distichous.

label: multistemmed
reason: Correct habit term (several stems from or near the base, no single trunk); branched is a reasonable parent and PATO has no such term.

label: tubercle-based
reason: Correct: a hair arising from an enlarged, wart-like multicellular base (pustulate-based). It inheres in the trichome, and the note already records that the stated stem or leaf is the whole the trichome belongs to.

label: camptodromous
definition: A pinnately veined quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's secondary veins not ending at the margin but curving upwards before it, either fading out or joining the secondary vein above.
bearers: leaf|secondary leaf vein|lateral leaf vein|vascular bundle
reason: In Hickey (1973) camptodromous covers all pinnate venation whose secondary veins do not reach the margin, including brochidodromous (joined in loops) and eucamptodromous. 'curving upwards near it' alone is too narrow. PATO:0001970 brochidodromous should then sit under this class.

label: polystichous
reason: Correct (arranged in many ranks); same parent as its sibling PATO:0001952 distichous; multifarious and many-ranked are standard synonyms.

label: intravaginal
reason: Correct grass and sedge innovation term; the exact counterpart of FLOPO:0991357 extravaginal, with the same parent.

label: stomatomorphic
reason: Fits the literal sense (stoma-shaped: two lips around a slit) and is limited to stigmas, as the source uses it. I could not confirm a standard glossary definition, so confidence is low.

label: gelatinous
reason: Correct; PATO has no gelatinous texture value (viscous is a viscosity value, and glutinous in PATO is an amylose composition). A French synonym follows earlier rows (e.g. biterné).

label: latrorse
reason: Correct, worded the same way as its siblings FLOPO:0991164 introrse and FLOPO:0991165 extrorse.

label: holomycotrophic
reason: Overlaps FLOPO:0991360 saprophytic, which already has the exact synonym 'mycoheterotrophic' and describes the same achlorophyllous, fungus-fed plants that floras call saprophytic. Two classes would split one set of annotations. Either merge them, or keep holomycotrophic as the correct term and make saprophytic a synonym or a deprecated class pointing to it.

label: semi-ellipsoid
reason: Correct and well formed; a half ellipsoid is convex, so the parent fits. PATO has ellipsoid but no half form.

label: upper
reason: Correct for a member's place in its series ('upper leaves'); PATO has only relational terms (distal to), which do not fit the 'state of the bearer' pattern.

label: lower
reason: Exact counterpart of upper; correct and well formed.

label: inner
reason: Correct for whorls and series ('inner tepals', 'inner bracts' of an involucre); well formed.

label: outer
reason: Exact counterpart of inner; correct and well formed.

label: lateral (sensu botany)
reason: The definition is right for a member of a series (lateral sepals or petals, as in orchids), but the related synonym 'lateral' will also match 'lateral inflorescences, buds, branches or veins', where lateral means arising from the side of an axis (axillary, not terminal). That is a second meaning. Match only on the series words (sepal, petal, tepal, lobe), or send 'lateral' + axis parts to FLOPO:0991000 axillary or PATO:0001193 lateral to.

label: median
reason: Synonyms do not fit. In floras, 'middle' (1,574 statements) mostly means midway along an axis ('middle cauline leaves', between upper and lower), not the median member between lateral ones. 'central' overlaps inner (FLOPO:0991378). FLOPO:0991299 medial (sensu botany) already has 'median' as a related synonym with another meaning. Either give 'middle' its own class (midway between the upper and lower members) or drop it, and remove 'median' from FLOPO:0991299.

label: porrect
definition: An orientation quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's projecting straight outwards from the surface or axis that bears it, neither ascending nor bent back or down.
reason: Glossaries give porrect as directed outward and forward, extended straight out. 'at about a right angle' clashes with its own synonym 'projecting forward' and is stricter than flora usage, where porrect spines are contrasted with ascending, spreading and descending ones.

label: obliquely truncate
reason: Correct child of PATO:0000936 truncated (the Carex perigynium beak orifice); well formed.

label: candelabriform
reason: Correct habit term (branches curving out and then erect, as in candelabra euphorbias and cacti); branched is the right parent.

label: epicortical
reason: Correct for the epicortical roots of mistletoes (Loranthaceae and Viscaceae), which run over the host bark and send haustoria into it; positional parent fits, like its siblings aerial and subterranean.

label: follicle-like
reason: Two meanings in one class. In floras 'fruit follicular' / 'follicle-like fruit' means the fruit is (or behaves as) a follicle, a fruit type defined by dehiscence along one suture, not a shape; that use should be a rule mapping to the bearer follicle fruit (PO:0030105, already in PO with synonym 'follicle'), not a shape quality of 'fruit'. The definition itself mixes appearance with dehiscence and carpel number, which are not shape. The exact synonym 'follicular' (= pertaining to or consisting of follicles) does not fit a shape class. If kept at all, restrict to non-fruit bearers (e.g. a capsule mericarp resembling a follicle) and drop 'follicular'; otherwise reject.

label: syconium ostiole
reason: Matches fig usage: the apical opening of the syconium closed by ostiolar bracts. Part of capitulum inflorescence is acceptable because PO has 'hypanthodium' as a synonym there. Related synonyms 'ostiole' and 'orifice' are correctly not exact.

label: endostome
reason: Correct moss usage: the inner peristome of a diplolepidous peristome, a basal membrane with segments and cilia inside the exostome. Part of peristome (PO:0030042) is right. Note the homonym: 'endostome' is also the opening of the inner integument of an ovule, so matching should be limited to moss-capsule contexts.

label: pinna rachis
exact_synonyms: secondary rachis|rachis of pinna|rachis of the pinnae|secondary rhachis|pinna rhachis|rachis secondaire|pinna axis
reason: Correct: the secondary axis of a bipinnate leaf. Stalk (PO:0025066) is the right parent, not leaf rachis (PO:0020055), because PO defines leaf rachis as the main axis. Synonyms fit.

label: sporocarp
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) of a heterosporous water fern (Marsileaceae, Salviniaceae) that is a closed, bean-, nut- or globe-shaped structure derived from a modified leaf segment or indusium, enclosing one or more sori (PO:0025359) and their sporangia.
reason: Not genus-differentia (no parent named). It is also too narrow: Salviniaceae sporocarps are soft and thin-walled, each holding a single sorus, so 'hard' applies only to Marsileaceae. 'sporocarpe' (French) is better as a language synonym than an English exact one.

label: corolla plica
reason: Correct Gentiana/Gentianaceae usage: the folded tissue between corolla lobes. Parent and part-of are appropriate and the synonyms fit.

label: lithocyst
reason: Correct: a cell (idioblast, PO:0000283) containing a cystolith of calcium carbonate on a cellulose stalk, as in Acanthaceae, Urticaceae and Moraceae. Putting 'cystolith' as a related synonym rather than exact is right, since floras say 'cystoliths visible' when they mean the lithocysts.

label: perispore
reason: Correct fern usage: the outer wall layer outside the exospore, laid down from tapetal (periplasmodial) material. Plant structure is a broad parent but not wrong. 'perine' is rightly related, since it is also used for pollen.

label: perigynium beak
reason: Correct Carex usage: the beak above the body of the perigynium, often bidentate at the orifice. Parent and part-of (perigynium, PO:0009044) are right.

label: pseudoparaphyllium
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) of a moss gametophore axis (PO:0030020) that is a small leaf-like, scale-like or filamentous outgrowth found only around a branch primordium or at the base of a branch, not scattered between the leaves.
reason: Wrong parent. Plant epidermis (PO:0005679) is a tissue layer, but a pseudoparaphyllium is a discrete multicellular outgrowth (often leaf-like), so it should sit under cardinal organ part, like the other appendage classes here. The definition also lacks genus-differentia form; the text above fixes both.

label: stelidium
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) that is one of a usually paired set of tooth- or arm-like projections at the apex or sides of the gynostemium (FLOPO:0986015) of an orchid flower, flanking the anther, as in Bulbophyllum and Pleurothallidinae.
reason: The meaning is right, but 'one of a usually paired tooth- or arm-like projection' is ungrammatical. Also check the related synonym 'stegidia': it is not a standard term and looks like an OCR or spelling error, so it should be dropped.

label: connective appendage
exact_synonyms: connective appendages|connective appendix|anther appendage|anther appendix|anther tail
reason: The class and definition are correct (Melastomataceae, Violaceae, and the apical appendage in Asteraceae), but the exact synonym 'anther tail' does not fit. Anther tails (caudate anthers in Asteraceae) are basal extensions of the thecae, not of the connective. Remove it, or make it a separate bearer; keep the other synonyms.

label: rhizophore
definition: A plant axis (PO:0025004) that is leafless and usually unbranched, arises at a branching point of the stem of Selaginella and grows down to the substrate, where it produces roots at its tip.
reason: Not genus-differentia (the parent is not named). Note that 'rhizophore' is also used for the stilt roots of Rhizophora and for the root-bearing organs of Dioscorea; text matches outside Selaginella should not be mapped here.

label: limbidium
reason: Correct moss usage: a leaf border of differentiated elongate cells. PO leaf margin (PO:0020128) is part of leaf (PO:0025034), which covers non-vascular leaves, so the parent is fine. The exact synonym 'leaf border' is somewhat broad (it could match a hyaline or toothed border) and is better made related.

label: stipule lobe
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) that is a free lobe, segment or fimbria of a divided stipule (PO:0020041).
exact_synonyms: stipule lobes|stipule segment|stipule segments|stipular lobe|lobe of stipule
reason: The meaning is right but the parent is not named; the text above puts it in genus-differentia form.

label: hyaline cell
definition: A native plant cell (PO:0025606) of a non-vascular leaf (PO:0025075) that is large, colourless, dead and empty at maturity and holds water, often strengthened by fibrils and perforated by pores, and that alternates with or encloses narrow living chlorophyllose cells, as in Sphagnum and the Leucobryaceae.
reason: Too narrow. Moss floras also use 'hyaline cells' (leucocysts) in Leucobryum and its relatives, and the related synonym 'leucocyst' is actually a Leucobryaceae term. One sentence in genus-differentia form is better than two.

label: spine shield
reason: Correct succulent Euphorbia usage: a horny pad bearing the spines that may join into a continuous horny margin. Parent and part-of (stem) are right.

label: style head
reason: Correct Apocynaceae usage (style head / pistil head / clavuncle), united with the anthers in the gynostegium. The synonyms are standard in Apocynaceae floras.

label: pseudostaminode
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) that is a lobe or appendage of the staminal tube or cup, standing between the filaments and not derived from a stamen, as in many Amaranthaceae.
reason: The meaning is right (Amaranthaceae interstaminal lobes), but the parent is not named; 'staminal tube or cup' covers both usages.

label: column foot
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) that is a forward extension of the base of the gynostemium (FLOPO:0986015) of an orchid flower, to which the lateral sepals and often the lip are attached, the lateral sepals and the foot together forming a mentum.
reason: Not genus-differentia. The mentum is formed by the lateral sepals joined to the column foot; the lip is hinged at its tip.

label: infrastaminal scale
reason: The definition is fine (e.g. Cuscuta), but the exact synonym 'corolla scale' is too broad: it also covers the faucal scales (fornices) of Boraginaceae and corona-like scales at the throat. Move it to related synonyms.

label: loment segment
exact_synonyms: pod article|loment article|pod segment|joint of the pod|fruit article|fruit segment
reason: The definition is correct, but the exact synonyms 'fruit segment' and 'fruit article' are too broad: they also cover mericarps of schizocarps, segments of lomentaceous siliques and citrus segments. Keep 'loment article', 'pod article' and 'joint of the pod'; move the generic ones to related.

label: bladder trap
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) that is a small, hollow, usually stalked bladder developed from a leaf or leaf segment, with a mouth closed by a trapdoor bearing trigger hairs and glands, which catches small aquatic animals by suction, as in Utricularia.
reason: Factual fix: the trigger hairs on the door are not glandular; the glands are separate. Otherwise correct.

label: buttress root
reason: Correct: a plank buttress formed by eccentric secondary growth on the upper side of a superficial lateral root near the trunk base. Parent root and the synonyms fit. Minor wording ('joins the trunk to the ground') could be tightened, but it is acceptable.

label: perichaetium
reason: Matches standard bryological usage: the perichaetial leaves (PO:0030030 perichaetal bract) together with the archegonia they surround. Plant structure is a broad parent but not wrong.

label: phyllopodium
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) of a rhizome (PO:0004542) that is a short, persistent, stalk-like outgrowth to which the stipe of a fern leaf is articulated, and which remains on the rhizome after the leaf falls, as in Polypodiaceae and Oleandra.
reason: In fern glossaries and floras (e.g. Flora of China), phyllopodia are outgrowths of the rhizome to which the stipes are jointed. The current text puts the structure 'at the base of a fern leaf' and leaves it with no bearer. part_of should be rhizome (PO_0004542). The text also lacks PO identifiers.

label: supra-alar cell
reason: Matches moss glossary usage: the cells just above the alar cells at the basal leaf margin, often differentiated from the other laminal cells. The text has the genus and differentia and cites its identifiers.

label: outer ligule
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) of a leaf (PO:0025034) that is a rim or fringe of tissue on the abaxial side at the junction of the leaf sheath (PO:0020104) and the leaf lamina (PO:0020039), opposite the ligule (PO:0020105), as in bamboos and some other grasses.
reason: Meaning is correct (outer ligule = contraligule of bamboos). Only change: the text now cites PO identifiers, like the other rows.

label: mesochile
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) of an orchid labellum (FLOPO:0980978) that is the middle of three successive segments of the labellum, lying between the hypochile (FLOPO:0986030) and the epichile (FLOPO:0986029).
reason: Meaning is correct. 'Tripartite' can be misread as three lobes side by side. The mesochile is the middle segment from base to tip, not a side lobe. The text also lacks identifiers.

label: seed wing
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) of a seed (PO:0009010) that is a thin, flat, membranous outgrowth that aids wind dispersal, formed from the seed coat (PO:0009088) or, in conifers, from tissue of the ovuliferous scale (PO:0009027) that stays attached to the seed.
reason: Meaning is correct. The text lacked its genus and identifiers. 'Stays attached' explains why the conifer wing counts as part of the seed even though it comes from the scale.

label: lignotuber
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) of a stem (PO:0009047) that is a woody swelling at the stem base, at or below ground level, bearing many dormant buds and storing food reserves, from which the plant resprouts after fire or cutting, as in many Eucalyptus.
reason: A lignotuber is a swollen region of the stem base, not a whole shoot axis. Making it a shoot axis that is part of a stem (itself a shoot axis) is inconsistent. In PO, portions of a stem, such as shoot axis internode, are cardinal organ parts. Botanical meaning and synonyms are fine; 'burl' is rightly only a related synonym, since trunk burls also occur above ground.

label: calyx limb
definition: A collective organ part structure (PO:0025269) composed of the distal portions of the sepals (PO:0009031) of a fused calyx (PO:0025582), above the calyx tube (FLOPO:0986011).
reason: Correct, and modelled on corolla limb (FLOPO:0986012). The final list 'entire, truncate, toothed or lobed' gives the limb's possible qualities, not what defines it, and should go. Consider making calyx limb and corolla limb subclasses of perianth limb (FLOPO:0986104), as calyx tube is of perianth tube.

label: floral disc lobe
reason: A clear genus-differentia definition with the right bearer, floral disc (FLOPO:0986025). It is used like the other 'lobe' classes.

label: vaginant lamina
reason: The class and definition are correct (the sheathing duplicate base of Fissidens leaves). The problem is the exact synonyms 'vagrant lamina' and 'vagrant laminae': they are misspellings (OCR or typo) and do not fit as exact synonyms. Drop them, or keep them only as hidden text-mining labels.

label: involucre lobe
reason: Correct for the fused involucres of Euphorbia (cyathium), Nyctaginaceae and Eriogonum. The 'tooth' synonyms are acceptable.

label: stamen fascicle
definition: A collective plant organ structure (PO:0025007) that is part of an androecium (PO:0009061) and consists of a group of stamens (PO:0009029) borne together and usually connate at the base of their filaments, as in Hypericaceae, Clusiaceae, some Myrtaceae and Malvaceae s.l. (e.g. Tilia, Bombacoideae).
reason: Requiring connate filaments is too narrow: floras use 'stamens in fascicles' for groups that are only close together (e.g. Tilia, Dilleniaceae). Also, typical Malvoideae have a single staminal tube (FLOPO:0986013), not fascicles, so the Malvaceae example needs narrowing.

label: guide cell
reason: Matches bryological usage: the deuters are large cells in a median row of the costa, between the stereid bands. The bearer and identifiers are correct.

label: stomatal line
definition: A plant structure (PO:0009011) that is a single longitudinal row of stomatal complexes (PO:0002000) in the leaf epidermis (PO:0006016), as on conifer needles; several adjacent lines make up a stomatal band.
reason: Meaning is correct. Only change: the text now cites identifiers. Collective plant structure (PO_0025497) would be a more precise parent, since a line is a group of stomatal complexes, but plant structure is not wrong.

label: laminal cell
reason: The definition is correct for mosses. But the exact synonym 'leaf cells' is far too wide: as an exact synonym it would also match leaf cells of vascular plants. Make it a related synonym, or limit it to moss sources. 'lamina cells' has the same risk on a smaller scale.

label: spadix staminate zone
definition: A staminate zone of inflorescence (FLOPO:0986106) that is the portion of a spadix inflorescence (PO:0030120) bearing the staminate flowers (PO:0025600), together with the part of the spadix axis on which they are borne, as in Araceae.
exact_synonyms: male zone|staminate zone|male portion of spadix|spadix staminate part|staminate part of spadix|male zone of spadix|male part of spadix
reason: Overlaps FLOPO:0986106 (staminate zone of inflorescence), which already covers the spadix. It should be a subclass of that class. Its general exact synonyms 'staminate zone' and 'male zone' belong on FLOPO:0986106. Also, this text leaves out the spadix axis, but its pistillate twin (FLOPO:0986105) includes it; the two should match.

label: rostellum lobe
reason: Correct, with the right bearer, rostellum (FLOPO:0986017). The rostellum arms of Habenaria are a fitting example.

label: anther tube
reason: Correct: syngenesious anthers in Asteraceae and Lobelioideae. Its parent matches staminal tube. 'Syngenesious anthers' would fit better as a related synonym, because the word also carries the quality of being fused.

label: perianth limb
definition: A collective organ part structure (PO:0025269) composed of the expanded distal portions of the perianth members of a fused perianth (PO:0025580), above the perianth tube (FLOPO:0986010).
reason: Wrong parent. A limb is formed by several fused perianth members, so it is a collective organ part structure, as corolla limb (FLOPO:0986012) and calyx limb (FLOPO:0986093) already are. A cardinal organ part belongs to a single organ. Calyx limb and corolla limb should then become its subclasses.

label: spadix pistillate zone
reason: Correct for Araceae. Pistillate flower could be cited as PO:0025599. If a general 'staminate zone of inflorescence' is kept, it needs a matching general pistillate class (for example for Typha), which would take the generic synonyms 'pistillate zone' and 'female zone'.

label: staminate zone of inflorescence
reason: Correct general class (Araceae spadix, Typha spike). It should become the parent of FLOPO:0986101 and take that class's generic synonyms. See that item.

label: emergence
definition: A plant structure (PO:0009011) that is a multicellular outgrowth formed from the plant epidermis (PO:0005679) together with underlying tissue, such as a prickle (PO:0025169) or the stalked glands of Drosera, as distinct from a trichome (PO:0000282), which arises from the epidermis alone.
reason: Matches the standard anatomical definition. The new text cites identifiers and names prickle (PO:0025169), which would logically be a kind of emergence.

label: hastula
reason: Correct palm usage: a flap or crest, adaxial or abaxial, at the junction of petiole and blade. The bearer and identifiers are right.

label: aerophore
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) of a vascular leaf (PO:0009025) of a fern that is a pale, often swollen outgrowth or line of aerating tissue at the base of a pinna or along the stipe, serving for gas exchange, as in Thelypteridaceae.
reason: Meaning is correct. The text calls PO:0009025 'fern leaf', but that identifier is 'vascular leaf'. The label and identifier must match.

label: corolla throat
definition: A collective organ part structure (PO:0025269) that is the region of a fused corolla (PO:0025581) where the corolla tube (FLOPO:0985018) widens into the corolla limb (FLOPO:0986012), including the opening of the tube.
reason: Meaning is correct, but the throat is formed by all the fused petals together. It should be a collective organ part structure, like corolla limb (FLOPO:0986012), not part of a single organ. The text should also cite the tube and limb classes.

label: laesura
reason: Matches palynological and fern glossary usage: a scar on the proximal face, trilete or monolete, along which the spore opens. 'Commissure' is rightly only a related synonym.

label: corpusculum
definition: A plant structure (PO:0009011) that is a hard, dark, clip-like body secreted by the style head of the gynostegium (FLOPO:0986051) between two adjacent anthers, which, together with two translator arms, joins pollinia (FLOPO:0986016) of adjacent anthers into a pollinarium and clips it to a pollinator, as in Apocynaceae subfamily Asclepiadoideae.
reason: The corpusculum is a hardened secretion, not tissue, so 'multi-tissue plant structure' is the wrong genus. Use the same parent as pollinium (PO:0009011). The definition is not in genus-differentia form, and 'stigma head' should be 'style head' to match FLOPO's style head class. The synonyms are fine; it is correctly kept distinct from the orchid viscidium.

label: pedicel scar
reason: Correct genus-differentia definition, consistent with leaf scar (FLOPO:0986052, a cardinal organ part that is part of a shoot axis).

label: elater
definition: A plant cell (PO:0009002) of a liverwort sporangium (PO:0025094) that is elongated, dead at maturity and has spiral wall thickenings, lies among the spores and twists as its moisture content changes, so helping to loosen and disperse the spores.
reason: Not in genus-differentia form. Including hornworts is wrong: hornworts have pseudo-elaters, which are often multicellular and lack spiral thickenings. The definition should also be kept separate from the Equisetum 'elaters', which are ribbon-like bands of the spore wall, not cells, so that annotations of horsetail spores do not map here.

label: faucal appendage
definition: A multi-tissue plant structure (PO:0025496) that is an infolding or scale-like outgrowth of the corolla (PO:0009059) in the corolla throat, opposite a corolla lobe, that partly closes the mouth of the corolla tube, as in Boraginaceae.
reason: The class is sound but the exact synonym 'corolla appendage' is far too wide: it also covers coronas, spurs and lobe appendages, and would capture unrelated text. Move it out (at most related). The definition is also not in genus-differentia form. Part_of could be the FLOPO corolla throat class rather than the whole corolla.

label: stipule scar
reason: Correct and well formed, parallel to leaf scar. 'cicatrice stipulaire' is a French exact synonym and belongs in the French synonym column.

label: stereid band
reason: Matches bryological usage: bands of stereids dorsal and/or ventral to the guide cells in the costa. Genus-differentia form, cites PO stereid.

label: pseudoperianth
reason: Correct: a post-fertilization sheath of thallus tissue (Marchantia, also Fossombronia), correctly kept apart from the gametophyte perianth (PO:0030031). A narrower genus (multi-tissue plant structure) would also be defensible.

label: asexual propagule
definition: A plant structure (PO:0009011) that becomes detached from the parent plant and grows into a new individual without sexual reproduction, such as a gemma (PO:0025614), a bulbil, a brood body, a rhizoidal tuber or a deciduous branchlet.
reason: 'Brood body' is a kind of asexual propagule, not the same thing, so it should not be an exact synonym (it would make PO gemma and brood cells collide with this class). The definition lacks the parent ID. PO gemma (PO:0025614), and FLOPO bulbil and turion, are natural subclasses. The related synonym 'propagule' is also a PO synonym of fruit, so keep it related only.

label: floret callus
reason: Standard grass usage (base of the lemma plus a rachilla segment, the point where the floret breaks away). Well formed. Keeping 'callus' as a related synonym only is right, since PO 'plant callus' is tissue culture.

label: chlorophyllose cell
definition: A plant cell (PO:0009002) of a non-vascular leaf (PO:0025075) that is narrow, living and contains chloroplasts and lies between large dead hyaline cells (FLOPO:0986077), forming a network in Sphagnum or a layer between layers of hyaline cells in Leucobryaceae.
reason: Too narrow: Leucobryum and its relatives also have chlorophyllose cells (chlorocysts) between hyaline cells. 'Its cross-sectional shape ... are diagnostic' is a usage note, not part of a definition. Its partner class, hyaline cell, sits under native plant cell (PO:0025606); one of the two parents should be aligned.

label: clinandrium
reason: The definition is correct and well formed (anther bed at the column apex). However, the exact synonym 'clinandrium-hood' names only the raised margin of the clinandrium, not the whole cavity, so it should be removed or made related. 'anther bed' and 'androclinium' are fine.

label: dorsal lamina
reason: Correct Fissidens usage: the dorsal lamina lies on the abaxial side of the costa, opposite the vaginant laminae (FLOPO:0986095). Genus-differentia form.

label: endocarp condyle
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) of an endocarp (PO:0009086) that is an intrusion of the endocarp into the locule, around which the seed is curved, and that is often hollow or perforate, as in Menispermaceae.
reason: The meaning is right (Menispermaceae condyle) but the text lacks the genus and PO identifiers.

label: endostome basal membrane
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) of an endostome (FLOPO:0986064) that is its continuous, membranous lower part, from which the endostome segments and cilia arise, in the peristome (PO:0030042) of a moss capsule.
reason: The meaning is right, but FLOPO already has endostome (FLOPO:0986064), so part_of should point to it rather than to the whole peristome, and the definition should cite it. Also, curation/flopo-trait-phenotype-classification.tsv lists FLOPO_0986125 with the label 'endostome'; check that this is not a mapping error.

label: phyllid lamella
reason: Correct (Polytrichaceae, Pterygoneurum and other Pottiaceae). Genus-differentia form with PO identifiers.

label: nodal diaphragm
reason: The definition is good. However, bare 'diaphragm' as an exact synonym would also capture the diaphragmed (chambered) pith of Juglans and similar stems and the transverse septa of Juncus leaves, which are not nodal. Move 'diaphragm' to related synonyms.

label: leaf vein axil
reason: Matches glossary usage (vein axils bearing hairs or domatia) and is well formed. Treating it as a region of the lamina, not a PO anatomical space (PO:0025224 axil, which is shoot–leaf), is appropriate.

label: cirrus
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) of a leaf rachis (PO:0020055) that is its long, leafless, whip-like, non-coiling extension beyond the uppermost leaflets, armed with grapnel-like spines, by which climbing palms (rattans) attach to supports.
reason: The cirrus is the end part of the rachis, not a kind of rachis: a leaf has one rachis, which includes the cirrus. It should be a cardinal organ part that is part of the leaf rachis, like the other 'part of' classes. The meaning is right and correctly kept distinct from the flagellum, which is a modified inflorescence.

label: syconium
reason: The definition is correct and well formed. A note for consistency: syconium ostiole (FLOPO:0986063) is part of capitulum inflorescence (PO:0030121), and PO lists 'hypanthodium' as a capitulum synonym. The ostiole should now be part of this class.

label: anther theca appendage
exact_synonyms: thecal appendage|theca appendage|anther spur|basal appendage of theca
reason: Correct (Acanthaceae theca spurs and tails), well formed, and distinct from connective appendage.

label: carpopodium
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) of a cypsela (FLOPO:0986053) that is a distinct ring or pad of differentiated, often sclerified cells at its base, by which the fruit is attached to the receptacle and from which it separates.
reason: The meaning is right (Asteraceae carpopodium) but the text lacks the PO and FLOPO identifiers. 'basal callus' is better as a related synonym than an exact one.

label: floral spur
definition: A multi-tissue plant structure (PO:0025496) of a flower (PO:0009046) that is a hollow, tubular or sac-like extension of a petal, sepal, labellum or corolla, often containing nectar.
reason: PO already has petal spur (PO:0025511, a cardinal organ part) and corolla spur (PO:0025512, a collective organ part structure). As an umbrella class this must sit high enough to take both as subclasses; under cardinal organ part it cannot contain corolla spur.

label: velum
reason: Correct Isoetes usage and well formed.

label: teniola
definition: A portion of plant tissue (PO:0009007) of a non-vascular leaf (PO:0025075) that is a longitudinal band of elongate, thick-walled, often hyaline cells within the leaf lamina, between the costa (PO:0030072) and the margin, as in Calymperaceae.
reason: The meaning is right but the text lacks the identifiers and genus-differentia form, and puts the taxon in the middle of the definition rather than as an example.

label: tegula
reason: The definition is correct (Dressler's tegula: a stipe from the epidermis of the rostellum). However, the exact synonym 'stipe of pollinarium' is wider: the hamulus is the other kind of orchid stipe. It should be removed or made related. 'tegular stipe' is fine.

label: anther wing
reason: The class and its definition are correct. In Asclepiadoideae (and Secamonoideae) each anther has hard, membranous to cartilaginous side wings, and two neighbouring wings frame the guide rail (the stigmatic slit) that leads the pollinator's leg to the corpusculum. The parent (cardinal organ part, part of anther) fits. The problem is the exact synonym 'guide rail wing': the guide rail is the slit formed by a PAIR of wings from neighbouring anthers, not one wing, and the phrase is not standard glossary usage. Move it to related synonyms or drop it. 'anther flange' can stay as an exact synonym.

label: false vein
reason: This matches fern usage: false veins (false veinlets, spurious veins) are strands of long, often thick-walled cells in the leaf blade that are not connected to the true veins and carry no vascular tissue. They are typical of Hymenophyllaceae (e.g. Didymoglossum, Crepidomanes, often running inside the margin) and some Adiantum (Pteridaceae). The definition follows the genus-differentia form, and the parent and part-of (cardinal organ part of a phyllome lamina; leaf lamina is a kind of phyllome lamina) fit. 'false veinlet' and the French 'fausse nervure' work as exact synonyms, and 'pseudovein' fits as a related one. The phrase 'not connected to the vascular system and without vascular tissue' is slightly repetitive but correct.

label: fruit beak
reason: The definition is botanically correct: the beak (rostrum) is a narrowed, prolonged tip of the fruit. In Brassicaceae it is the seedless top of the silique, in Cyperaceae it comes from the persistent style base, in Lactuceae it is the stalk-like neck of the cypsela, and the stylar beak of Geraniaceae also fits. A cardinal organ part is the right parent, rather than PO 'fruit distal end' (PO_0008001), which is a region and not a projection. The problem is that 'achene beak' is listed as an exact synonym. It names only the beak of an achene or cypsela, so it is narrower than 'fruit beak' (silique beaks are not achene beaks) and should be a narrow synonym. 'beak', 'rostrum' and 'bec' are rightly related synonyms, since they also apply to perigynium, keel and operculum beaks.
